title: Cheese sauce (Mornay)
desc: Béchamel + cheese, stirred in off the heat. The milk-free version uses the cream-and-water béchamel.
reheat: Warm gently with a splash of liquid; don't boil.
variant: The milk-free version: make the béchamel with 150 ml cream + 350 ml water instead of milk.
trouble: Cheese added on the heat or the sauce boiled — add cheese off the heat, a handful at a time.

steps.t: Make a béchamel: cook the butter and flour 2 minutes, whisk in the warm milk in three goes, simmer 5 minutes.
steps.w: The roux-thickened base holds melted cheese without it splitting.
steps.m: Skipping the 5-minute simmer — floury taste.
steps.img: smooth white sauce being whisked in a saucepan

steps.t: Take the pan off the heat. Stir in the parmesan a handful at a time until melted, then the mustard and nutmeg.
steps.w: Cheese proteins tighten and squeeze out fat above ~80 °C — off the heat they melt smoothly.
steps.m: Boiling after the cheese goes in — grainy sauce.
steps.img: grated cheese melting into a white sauce off the heat

steps.t: Taste and add salt only if needed — the cheese is salty.
steps.w: Season last.
steps.m: Salting early.
steps.img: spoon of golden cheese sauce

title: Red-wine pan sauce, alcohol-free (stock + red wine vinegar)
desc: Made in the steak pan from the brown bits, for both portions in one pan: stock and a little red wine vinegar do the job of the wine — same technique, no alcohol.
variant: With wine (never in the other portion): in a second small pan, boil 60 ml red wine with half the shallots 1–2 minutes until almost gone, then use 60 ml less stock and leave out half the vinegar for that portion.
trouble: Reduce longer before the butter goes in.
Butter added while boiling — take the pan off the heat, swirl in cold butter.
The fond was burnt (black) — start fresh in a clean pan.

steps.t: After searing steak, move it to rest. Pour off all but 1 tsp fat. On medium heat, cook the shallot in the pan 1 minute, scraping.
steps.w: The shallot picks up the brown bits (fond) and adds sweetness.
steps.c: Shallot soft, pan bottom brown, not black.
steps.m: Black bits in the pan — that's burnt, not fond.
steps.img: diced shallot softening in a pan with browned steak bits

steps.t: Make the sauce: pour in all the stock and the red wine vinegar, add the thyme, scrape the brown bits off the bottom with a wooden spoon and boil until reduced by about half.
steps.w: Reduction concentrates gelatine and flavour so the sauce gets body.
steps.c: Coats a spoon; big slow bubbles.
steps.m: Stopping too early — thin sauce.
steps.img: dark pan sauce reducing, big glossy bubbles

steps.t: Off the heat, swirl in the cold butter a cube at a time. Add the steak's resting juices, taste, salt.
steps.w: Cold butter emulsifies into the reduction and makes it glossy (monter au beurre).
steps.m: Butter into a boiling sauce — it goes greasy.
steps.img: glossy dark pan sauce poured over sliced steak

title: Peppercorn sauce (no brandy)
desc: Steakhouse classic: crushed black pepper, stock reduction and cream, made in the steak pan.
reheat: Warm gently; add a splash of stock if thick.
trouble: Simmer another minute — cream thickens as it reduces.
Heat too high for too long — whisk in a spoon of stock.

steps.t: Crush the peppercorns coarsely in a mortar or under a pan.
steps.w: Coarse pieces give bursts of heat; fine pepper turns the sauce grey and harsh.
steps.m: Using ready-ground pepper.
steps.img: black peppercorns coarsely crushed in a mortar and pestle

steps.t: In the steak pan (fat poured off), melt the butter, cook the shallot and pepper 1 minute.
steps.w: Toasting pepper in fat releases its aroma.
steps.m: Burning the pepper — keep it moving.
steps.img: shallots and crushed pepper sizzling in butter in a steak pan

steps.t: Pour in the stock, scrape up the brown bits and boil until reduced by half.
steps.w: Deglazing turns the fond into sauce; reducing builds body.
steps.m: Not scraping — flavour left in the pan.
steps.img: stock deglazing a pan with peppercorns

steps.t: Add the cream and mustard, simmer 2 minutes until it coats a spoon. Add the steak juices, salt to taste.
steps.w: 35% cream can simmer without splitting and thickens as it reduces.
steps.c: Coats a spoon, pale coffee colour.
steps.m: Using light cream — it splits.
steps.img: creamy peppercorn sauce simmering in a pan

title: Beurre blanc (alcohol-free)
desc: A shallot and vinegar reduction whisked with cold butter into a light, tangy sauce for fish. Classic recipes add white wine — here vinegar and water do the job.
reheat: Doesn't reheat — make just before serving.
trouble: It got too hot — take it off, whisk in a tablespoon of cold water or an ice cube.
Too cold — warm gently while whisking.
Whisk in a little more butter.
goes: Salmon, sea bass, sea bream, asparagus.

steps.t: Simmer the shallot, vinegar and water in a small saucepan until only about 2 tablespoons remain.
steps.w: The reduction gives acidity and the water base that holds the butter.
steps.c: Shallots glistening in a tablespoon or two of liquid.
steps.m: Reducing to dry — it burns.
steps.img: shallots reducing in vinegar in a small saucepan

steps.t: Turn the heat to its lowest. Whisk in the cold butter one cube at a time, adding the next only when the last has nearly melted.
steps.w: Cold butter melts slowly into an emulsion; it must never boil.
steps.m: Butter all at once or heat too high — oily split.
steps.img: cold butter cubes being whisked into a reduction, pale creamy sauce

steps.t: Season with lemon and salt. Strain out the shallots if you want it smooth. Serve straight away.
steps.w: It holds only while warm — like a hollandaise without eggs.
steps.m: Leaving it on the hob.
steps.img: beurre blanc spooned over a fillet of white fish

title: Gravy from roast-chicken juices
desc: Pan juices + a little flour + stock = proper gravy, no granules.
left: Freeze in cubes for the next roast.
trouble: Cook the flour in the fat a minute longer before the stock.
Simmer longer, or a corn-flour slurry.

steps.t: Lift the roast out to rest. Tilt the tray and spoon off all but about 1 tbsp of fat, leaving the brown juices.
steps.w: Too much fat makes greasy gravy; the dark juices are the flavour.
steps.c: Brown sticky juices and 1 tbsp fat.
steps.m: Pouring the juices away with the fat.
steps.img: spooning fat from a roasting tray leaving brown juices

steps.t: Put the tray over medium heat, sprinkle in the flour and whisk 1 minute.
steps.w: The fat and flour make a quick roux in the tray.
steps.m: Lumps from dumping flour in one spot — sprinkle evenly.
steps.img: flour being whisked into pan juices in a roasting tray on the hob

steps.t: Whisk in the hot stock gradually, scraping the tray, add thyme and simmer 4–5 minutes.
steps.w: Stock dissolves the roasting bits; simmering thickens the starch.
steps.m: Cold stock all at once.
steps.img: gravy simmering in a roasting tray

steps.t: Add the resting juices from the meat, season, and pour through a sieve into a warm jug.
steps.w: Straining gives a smooth gravy.
steps.m: Over-salting — stock is already salty.
steps.img: smooth gravy poured into a jug through a sieve

title: Two green sauces: basil pesto & chimichurri
desc: Same idea, two directions: Italian pesto (basil, pine nuts, parmesan) and Argentine chimichurri (parsley, oregano, vinegar, chilli) for steak.
left: Freeze pesto in ice-cube trays; chimichurri on eggs.
trouble: Blended too long (heat) — pulse briefly; cover the top with a film of oil.
Over-processed olive oil — stir the oil in by hand at the end.
goes: Pesto: pasta, roast cauliflower, chicken. Chimichurri: steak, lamb, grilled halloumi.

steps.t: Toast the pine nuts in a dry pan on medium-low, shaking, 2 minutes.
steps.w: Toasting brings out nutty oils.
steps.m: Walking away — they burn in seconds.
steps.img: pine nuts toasting golden in a dry pan

steps.t: Pesto: pulse the basil leaves, pine nuts, 1 garlic clove, parmesan and a pinch of salt in the blender to a rough paste.
steps.w: Short pulses cut the leaves without heating them.
steps.m: Running the blender non-stop — dark, bitter pesto.
steps.img: basil leaves pine nuts and parmesan in a blender jug

steps.t: Stir in 70 ml olive oil and the lemon by hand. Spoon into a jar and cover with a thin layer of oil.
steps.w: Stirring the oil in by hand keeps it from turning bitter; the oil layer stops browning.
steps.m: Leaving it uncovered — it darkens.
steps.img: bright green pesto in a glass jar with a layer of olive oil

steps.t: Chimichurri: finely chop the parsley and the other garlic clove by hand or with 3–4 quick pulses.
steps.w: Chimichurri should be chunky, not a purée.
steps.m: Blending it to a smooth paste.
steps.img: finely chopped parsley and garlic on a board

steps.t: Mix with oregano, vinegar, chilli, the remaining 50 ml oil and salt. Rest 10 minutes before serving.
steps.w: Resting lets the vinegar soften the garlic and the herbs flavour the oil.
steps.c: Loose, oily, bright green with red flecks.
steps.m: Serving it straight away — it tastes raw.
steps.img: chimichurri sauce in a bowl next to sliced grilled steak

title: Indian-style curry base
desc: Onions cooked down slowly, ginger, garlic, spices, tomato. Freeze it in portions and a curry takes 15 minutes.
reheat: Simmer, then add meat, veg or chickpeas.
left: Freeze 250 ml portions — each makes a curry for two.
trouble: Fry the spices in oil a full minute before the tomato goes in.
Onions on too high heat — add a splash of water and lower it.

steps.t: Cook the onions in the oil with a pinch of salt on medium for 20 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden.
steps.w: Slowly browned onions are the sweetness and body of the sauce.
steps.c: Soft, jammy, golden brown, about a third of the starting volume.
steps.m: Rushing on high heat — burnt edges, raw middles.
steps.img: deep golden caramelised onions in a wide pan

steps.t: Add the garlic and ginger and cook 2 minutes.
steps.w: They need only a short fry to lose their raw bite.
steps.m: Adding garlic at the start with the onions — it burns.
steps.img: grated ginger and garlic stirred into golden onions

steps.t: Add cumin, turmeric, paprika, garam masala and chilli; stir 1 minute.
steps.w: Spices release their flavour in hot fat (blooming), not in water.
steps.c: Spices darken slightly and smell toasted.
steps.m: Burning them — if they smell acrid, lower the heat.
steps.img: ground spices toasting with onions in a pan

steps.t: Add the tomatoes, water and salt; simmer 10 minutes, then blend smooth.
steps.w: Simmering marries the flavours; blending gives a restaurant-smooth sauce.
steps.c: Thick, glossy, deep orange-red; oil shining at the edges.
steps.m: Blending hot sauce in a full, closed blender — fill half and vent it.
steps.img: smooth orange curry sauce in a blender and pan

title: Mushroom cream sauce
desc: Well-browned mushrooms, garlic, thyme, stock and cream. No wine needed.
reheat: Warm gently with a splash of stock.
left: Spoon over chicken or stir through pasta.
trouble: Pan too full or not hot enough — cook in two batches.
Simmer a minute or two longer.

steps.t: Heat the oil and half the butter on high. Add the mushrooms in one layer and leave them 3 minutes before stirring.
steps.w: Mushrooms are mostly water; high heat and space evaporate it so they brown instead of stewing.
steps.c: Golden brown edges, pan dry, squeaky sound gone.
steps.m: Salting at the start or crowding the pan — grey, wet mushrooms.
steps.img: sliced mushrooms browning in a hot pan

steps.t: Lower to medium, add the rest of the butter, garlic and thyme for 1 minute. Season with salt.
steps.w: Salt now, once browned.
steps.m: Burning the garlic.
steps.img: garlic and thyme with browned mushrooms

steps.t: Add the stock, scrape, reduce by half, then the cream. Simmer 2–3 minutes until it coats a spoon. Pepper.
steps.w: Stock deglazes, cream thickens as it reduces.
steps.m: Boiling hard for long — it can split.
steps.img: creamy mushroom sauce simmering in a pan

title: Beef jus (no wine)
desc: Reduced beef stock with shallot, thyme and a little balsamic — the thin, intense sauce of steakhouses and roast beef.
trouble: Keep reducing, or a teaspoon of corn-flour slurry.
Use low-salt stock; reduce less, or add water and a squeeze of lemon.

steps.t: Brown the shallots in the oil in a saucepan on medium-high, 4 minutes.
steps.w: Browning adds roasted sweetness.
steps.m: Pale shallots — little flavour.
steps.img: sliced shallots browning in a saucepan

steps.t: Add the stock, thyme and balsamic; boil steadily until reduced to about a third (around 200 ml).
steps.w: Reducing stock concentrates its gelatine, which gives jus body without flour.
steps.c: Syrupy, coats a spoon thinly, deep brown.
steps.m: Using a salty cube and reducing it — far too salty. Use low-salt stock.
steps.img: beef stock reducing to a dark glossy jus in a saucepan

steps.t: Strain, then whisk in the butter off the heat.
steps.w: A little butter gives shine.
steps.m: Boiling after the butter.
steps.img: dark glossy jus poured over sliced steak

title: Béarnaise (no wine)
desc: Hollandaise's steakhouse cousin: a tarragon, shallot and vinegar reduction, then yolks and butter.
reheat: Whisk over warm water; never direct heat.
trouble: Whisk 1 tbsp hot water in a clean bowl and slowly whisk the split sauce into it.
Too hot — sieve and keep it off the heat more.

steps.t: Simmer the vinegar, water, shallot, half the tarragon and the pepper until about 2 tablespoons remain. Strain and cool slightly.
steps.w: The reduction carries the flavour and the acid that steadies the emulsion.
steps.m: Reducing to nothing.
steps.img: tarragon shallot vinegar reduction in a small pan

steps.t: Whisk the yolks with the reduction in a bowl over barely simmering water until thick and pale, 2–3 minutes.
steps.w: Gentle heat thickens the yolks into a foam that can hold butter.
steps.c: Ribbons when the whisk is lifted.
steps.m: Water boiling hard — scrambled yolks.
steps.img: egg yolks whisked to a thick foam over steam

steps.t: Off the heat, whisk in the warm butter drop by drop, then in a thin stream. Stir in the remaining tarragon and salt.
steps.w: Slow fat addition creates a stable emulsion.
steps.c: Thick and glossy with green flecks.
steps.m: Pouring the butter fast — it splits.
steps.img: glossy bearnaise with tarragon flecks in a bowl

title: Aioli
desc: Garlic mayonnaise: an egg yolk and olive oil emulsion. By hand or with a stick blender in a jar.
trouble: Start again with a fresh yolk and add the split mix to it drop by drop.
Extra virgin oil blended hard turns bitter — use half sunflower oil.

steps.t: Use eggs from a fresh, in-date box (raw yolk). Put the yolk, garlic paste, mustard, half the lemon and salt in a tall jar.
steps.w: Yolk and mustard are the emulsifiers that hold the oil.
steps.m: Fridge-cold yolk — harder to emulsify.
steps.img: egg yolk garlic and mustard in a tall glass jar

steps.t: Mix both oils in a jug. Blend (or whisk) while adding oil a few drops at a time for the first quarter, then a thin stream.
steps.w: The first drops form the emulsion; once it holds, it takes oil faster.
steps.m: Adding oil too fast at the start — it stays runny.
steps.img: stick blender making thick aioli in a jar

steps.t: Season with the rest of the lemon and salt. Keep covered in the fridge, max 3 days.
steps.w: Raw-egg sauces are kept cold and eaten fresh.
steps.m: Leaving it out on the table for hours.
steps.img: bowl of aioli with a spoon

title: Romesco
desc: Catalan blender sauce of roasted red peppers, toasted almonds, garlic and sherry vinegar.
left: Spread in a wrap, toss with roast veg.
trouble: Blend in a spoon of water.
goes: Grilled fish, chicken, roast vegetables, halloumi.

steps.t: Toast the almonds in a dry pan, shaking, 3–4 minutes.
steps.w: Toasted nuts taste deeper and thicken the sauce.
steps.m: Burning them.
steps.img: almonds toasting in a dry pan

steps.t: Blend the peppers, almonds, garlic, smoked paprika, vinegar, chilli and salt; drizzle in the oil while blending.
steps.w: Almonds give body; vinegar and smoked paprika give the Spanish character.
steps.m: Blending to a thin purée — keep some texture.
steps.img: brick-red romesco in a blender

steps.t: Taste: add vinegar or salt until it tastes bright.
steps.w: Season at the end.
steps.m: Serving it under-seasoned.
steps.img: bowl of romesco next to grilled vegetables

title: Salsa verde
desc: Italian green sauce: parsley, capers, anchovy, lemon, olive oil. Sharp and salty — lifts any grilled meat or fish.
left: Stir into yogurt for a dip.
variant: Vegetarian: leave out the anchovy, add 1 more tsp capers.
trouble: Pulse less, or chop by hand.

steps.t: Pulse the parsley, capers, anchovy, garlic and mustard in the blender until finely chopped.
steps.w: Anchovy melts in and gives savoury depth, not fishiness.
steps.m: Over-blending.
steps.img: parsley capers and anchovies in a blender jug

steps.t: Stir in the lemon juice, zest and olive oil by hand. Taste — it should be sharp and salty.
steps.w: Stirring the oil by hand keeps it from turning bitter.
steps.m: Adding salt — capers and anchovy are salty already.
steps.img: bright green salsa verde in a small bowl

title: Tahini sauce
desc: The Mediterranean taverna dip: tahini, lemon, garlic and water. It seizes, then turns creamy — that's normal.
left: Dressing for roast cauliflower and bowls.
trouble: Thick and clumpy after adding lemon
Keep whisking and add water a spoon at a time — it loosens and goes creamy.
More lemon and a pinch of salt.
goes: Souvlaki, falafel, grilled halloumi, roast cauliflower.

steps.t: Stir the tahini jar well, then whisk the tahini with the lemon and garlic.
steps.w: Acid makes the sesame proteins tighten — it goes thick and clumpy at first.
steps.m: Thinking it failed — it is supposed to seize.
steps.img: tahini being whisked with lemon juice, thick paste

steps.t: Whisk in the cold water a spoon at a time until smooth and pale, like thick cream. Salt and parsley.
steps.w: Water loosens the emulsion into a creamy sauce.
steps.c: Pale cream colour, falls slowly from a spoon.
steps.m: All the water at once — it can go thin.
steps.img: smooth pale tahini sauce in a bowl with parsley

title: Garlic yogurt-dill sauce
desc: Thick yogurt, garlic, dill and lemon — a plain dill yogurt sauce. Tahini sauce is the yogurt-free alternative.
trouble: Use thick strained yogurt; drain a thin one in a sieve for 30 minutes.
Let it sit 30 minutes; next time grate less.
goes: Souvlaki, grilled chicken, lamb, roast veg.

steps.t: Mix the yogurt, garlic, dill, lemon and olive oil. Taste, salt.
steps.w: Resting 15 minutes lets the garlic flavour spread.
steps.m: Too much garlic — start with one clove.
steps.img: thick yogurt dill sauce in a bowl drizzled with olive oil

title: Sugar-free smoky BBQ sauce
desc: Passata, smoked paprika, cider vinegar, mustard, onion and garlic powder simmered thick. American BBQ flavour, no sugar or honey.
left: Brush on chicken, pulled pork, halloumi skewers.
goes: Pulled pork, chicken thighs, halloumi skewers.

steps.t: Whisk everything — passata, tomato paste, cider vinegar, mustard, smoked paprika, onion and garlic powder, cumin, chilli, soy sauce, salt and pepper — in a saucepan.
steps.w: Smoked paprika gives the 'grill' flavour; tomato paste brings natural sweetness without sugar.
steps.m: Adding sugar or honey out of habit.
steps.img: BBQ sauce ingredients whisked together in a saucepan

steps.t: Simmer uncovered on low 20 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick. Cover partly — it spits.
steps.w: Reduction thickens and mellows the vinegar.
steps.m: High heat — it splatters and catches.
steps.img: thick dark red BBQ sauce simmering

steps.t: Cool, pour into a clean jar, refrigerate.
steps.w: Acidic sauce keeps well chilled.
steps.m: Jar not clean.
steps.img: jar of homemade BBQ sauce

title: Avgolemono sauce
desc: Egg and lemon thickened with hot stock — the Greek way to make soup and sauces silky. The skill: tempering.
trouble: Stock added too fast or sauce boiled — sieve it; next time temper slowly.
Warm gently, stirring, until it coats a spoon (don't boil).
goes: Chicken, meatballs (giouvarlakia), stuffed vine leaves, soup.

steps.t: Whisk the eggs in a bowl until frothy, then whisk in the lemon and corn flour.
steps.w: Corn flour protects the eggs from curdling.
steps.m: Not whisking enough — streaks of white.
steps.img: eggs and lemon whisked frothy in a bowl

steps.t: Whisking constantly, add the hot stock one ladle at a time.
steps.w: Tempering raises the egg temperature slowly so it thickens instead of scrambling.
steps.m: Pouring all the stock in at once — scrambled egg.
steps.img: hot stock ladled slowly into egg-lemon mixture while whisking

steps.t: Pour back into the pan and stir over LOW heat 1–2 minutes until it coats a spoon. Do not boil. Salt.
steps.w: Above ~80 °C the eggs curdle.
steps.c: Silky, pale yellow, coats a spoon.
steps.m: Letting it bubble.
steps.img: silky pale yellow avgolemono sauce coating a spoon

title: Skordalia (almond version)
desc: Powerful garlic dip of almonds, a little potato, olive oil and vinegar.
trouble: Potato over-processed — mash the potato by hand, then fold in.
goes: Fried or grilled fish, beetroot, vegetables.

steps.t: Boil the potato in salted water until a knife slides in, 15 minutes. Drain and mash by hand.
steps.w: Mashing by hand keeps it fluffy; a blade makes potato gluey.
steps.m: Putting potato in the food processor.
steps.img: boiled potato being mashed in a bowl

steps.t: Process the almonds, garlic, vinegar and water to a fine paste, then drizzle in the oil.
steps.w: Almonds give body and creaminess.
steps.m: Not processing the almonds fine enough — gritty.
steps.img: almond garlic paste in a food processor

steps.t: Fold the almond paste into the mash by hand, season with salt.
steps.w: Folding keeps it light.
steps.m: Over-mixing.
steps.img: bowl of skordalia dip with olive oil

title: Ladolemono
desc: Olive oil, lemon and oregano whisked together — the dressing for grilled fish, chicken and greens.
trouble: Normal — whisk again before pouring, or add ½ tsp mustard to hold it.

steps.t: Whisk the lemon juice, mustard, oregano and salt, then whisk in the olive oil until cloudy and thick.
steps.w: Whisking breaks the oil into tiny droplets; mustard keeps them suspended.
steps.m: Just pouring it all in a jar without shaking.
steps.img: ladolemono dressing whisked in a small bowl
